findings.claim: Original PE initialized CRT SBH maximum allocation size at 00438674 is 0x1e0 (480 bytes), so a 120-byte workspace object is eligible for native small-block allocation without a synthetic threshold setting. Original editor entry 00424181 calls __heap_init 00424F00; no static executable callers of threshold setter 00424F90 were found.
findings.limitations: No static xref does not exclude external or indirect threshold modification; original full Win32 process CRT startup not executed.

findings.claim: Original 00424F00 creates CRT heap and calls native 00424FB0 for 4MiB reservation and 64KiB initial commit; with actual initialized 480-byte threshold unchanged, original malloc(120)/free use native SBH. On simulated initial 64KiB commit failure, original native routines request release of earlier reservation, destroy created CRT heap and return failure.
findings.limitations: Win32 HeapCreate/Destroy and VirtualAlloc/VirtualFree calls isolated with synthetic return values; real OS heap/VM bookkeeping not exercised.

findings.claim: Original i386 CRT allocator made 931 distinct concurrent 128-byte allocations across 32 pages with one additional 64KiB native commit request. Original free of all 931 made the empty-page counter reach 32, which triggered original 004252FD call to 00425180(16). It decommitted exactly 16 pages, indices 31 down through 16, leaving empty-page count 16 and those page descriptors at 0xff.
findings.limitations: VirtualAlloc/VirtualFree responses simulated; address of returned additional commit is synthetic; original Win32 process not executed. Prior wrong-address test fixture was rejected.

findings.claim: After natural decommit of pages 31..16, an explicit test invocation of original 00425180(16) decommitted the remaining empty pages and triggered original 00425120 release of the now-completely decommitted 4MiB region. Native 00424F40 then destroyed CRT heap without duplicate region release.
findings.limitations: This final 16-page decommit was explicitly invoked in a controlled test; it was NOT naturally triggered by original _free. OS VirtualFree/HeapDestroy calls were simulated.
